questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The nature and landscape in Iceland was a crucial factor in choosing my destination and as well as a good university.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall an amazing experience that I can only recommend to others. Not just going to Iceland, but the whole exchange experience where you get too meet new people and explore the culture and nature of the country with an open mind. Iceland was truly amazing and I am very happy with the friends I made here. The university was great, but I wish there were more biology courses available for exhange students in English.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Rather easy with the information on the University of Iceland website as well as the list of courses and descriptions combined with the introduction during the orientation days. Service desk was also of great help.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got assistance from the service desk in getting my student card as well as a map for the campus with which buildings  were important and they helped me with contacting the right people for coordinating courses and overlapping time schedules. Orientationdays were great with socialising and giving a campus tour although it could be a bit more extensive.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was rather difficult, but I had a contact through family that lives here and helped me by renting me a room.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Depending on how far away from campus it can be a bit difficult during late autumn and winter months as it can get very cold with the wind and ice on roads. So i recommend getting a bus pass if you live far from campus. Luckily the university gives a 50% discount on bus passes.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Difficult to get into student housing and quite expensive from what I have heard.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not too difficult. Just register at the service desk and get a student ID and confirm your arrival.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You arrive to Haskolatorg (main university building) and find the service desk where you show some picture ID and confirm that you have arrived. Thereafter you get a student ID number and can access the university intranet system.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Help from the international division in main university building and at the service desk in the same building. Although in the beginning of the semester and at the end it was very busy so difficult to get help in person.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I would say it is difficult to get all the classes you want as there are a lot of courses overlapping in time schedule. Therefore be prepared to change courses. I had to change three of my courses because of overlapping time schedules and one course that wasn't held because of lacking registration to the course.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would recommend at least two or more courses other than the ones you intend to take to make sure that you have some alternatives if needed. Registration at the university was easy enough, just make sure you bring some ID like passport or driverlicense.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Lacking in biology courses and environmental science courses.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Fish ecology was very difficult with heavy workload and other courses was easier eventhough they had more credits and less workload. So the credits in some courses didn't reflect the workload.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching is more personal with smaller classes and you get personally graded throughout the semester with tests, quizzes, a lot of presentations and groupwork. In UCPH it is mostly just final exams without many mandatory classes unlike University of Iceland.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Natural hazards: Physical Processes	LAN513M (6 ECTS)
French for Beginners I	FRA017G (5 ECTS)
Basic Icelandic I	ÍSE025G	(10 ECTS)
Climate Change	UAU107M (6 ECTS)
Fish Ecology	LÍF532M (6 ECTS)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Basic Icelandic was very fun and nice to learn especially if you are staying for more than one semester. I only took 1 semester but the class was very informative in both the icelandic culture, politics and language because of a great teacher (Roberto Luigi Pagani). Otherwise Fish Ecology was very informative with a lot of field work and hands on experience even with dry suit snorkling, but the workload was VERY heavy compared to only 6 ECTS.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I found out there wasn't any wifi at my housing and therefore I bought an eSIM which i filled with 100 GB of data for roaming throughout the month. This cost around 200 DKK a month.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was way more expensive than i thought. Just buying food for 2 days could easily cost up to 400 DKK. Busses (the only public ransportation) was also expensive with 30 DKK for just one trip. But luckily you can get 50% discount for students.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There wasn't many clubs or sports opportunities available but the university has a student cellar which is a really cool place to hang out with fussball table, music, bar, restaurant and many events throughout the month.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Would recommend attending the orientation days for social network and cool opportunities as well as going to the pools in Iceland. Furthermore attend the ESN events that they hold throughout the semester. This is both fun and you get to network.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go on trips in Iceland exploring the beautiful nature and seek out events by ESN as well as go to the pools. Truly amazing opportunities and some of the things that made my exchange memorable.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The pools in Reykjavik. Whale watching. The view from the big church in Reykjavik (Hallgrimskirkja). Trips to the south, north and westfjords of Iceland.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Somewhat easy and you can go to the pools which is a very local culture. However Icelandic people can seem like they mind their own buissness they open up and are very friendly when you get to know them. Do activities with them and you make friends and thereby trying the local culture through icelandic people.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Attend the orientation days in the beginning and go to ESN events as well as asking in the main exchange whatsapp group if people want to go on trips to see Iceland nature.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: That icelandic people seemed a bit closed and was a bit hard to get into conversation with but once you actually speak with them they were really friendly.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The pool culture was really nice and they party quite a lot which is nice for making friends. Also just a general outdoor oriented mindset.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Have a saving as it is quite expensive to go to study in iceland eventhough you get a bit larger Erasmus+ grant. 
Attend all the events and activities to make friends as they are priceless to make your exchange amazing.
Course grading and work is different from UCPH with a lot of graded presentations and groupwork as well as tests and quizzes.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Have a driver licence or make friends with somebody that has one to make sure you can go on trips to see the whole island with trips in the weekends.
Grocery shop in Bónus or Kronan as they are cheapest. Make food for multiple days to save money.
Get a bus pass if you live off campus.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends i made throughout the semester as well as the beatiful nature i got to experience here.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The different work from UCPH throughout the semester with a lot of ongoing grading and work. Timemanagement can be difficult with balancing socialising and keeping up with studies.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Go to Iceland to study for one semester, i can only recommend it! A beautiful country and amazing experiences awaits with nice people and incredible nature.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
